goal: `mc test <repo> <pr>` reads that repository's instruction for what to run, runs the tests the diff reaches, runs the gates the selector named beside them, and answers one question: is this change red? `mc test <repo> --full` runs the whole suite instead, which is the only place the state of main is a question at all.

The round does none of that today. It runs the same file list on **both** sides and calls the difference the verdict, so half the wall clock and most of the machinery exist to answer "was main already red?" — which Martin ruled on 2026-08-31 is not interesting at a merge. It reads `parsed?.files` from the selector's JSON and discards the `commands` beside them: on pull request #11158 that is six gates worth **20.0 s** — i18n three times, `sdk:check`, `css:lint`, `css:tokens` — that no round has run since `select` was declared. And the instruction for what to run lives in mc's own source rather than in the repository it describes.

The instruction is deliberately not "run `npm run ci`": measured at 554.7 s on that pull request, and ruled out the same day as too big. It is the selector's list plus the gates the selector names, run once.
contract: A round evaluates the diff. It does not run the baseline side, does not consult a standing red set, and does not ask whether main was already red — a test the change reaches is either green or the round is red. Ruled by Martin, 2026-08-31.

The verdict is short. What failed, and what ran. A session reading it should have nothing to weigh: caveats, reach sentences, blindness counts and comparison ages cost tokens and turn a yes/no into a judgement call. Diagnostics belong behind `--json`.

`mc test` never merges. `repo-gate.js` asserts against its own source that no merge call exists in it, and `mc merge` keeps paying for the measurement this verb performs rather than growing a second one.
The instruction is data about a repository, not logic in mc. This project adds no new hardcoded knowledge about a named repository to mc's source; it moves what is already there behind a declaration.
out_of_scope: What memoro selects, and how fast memoro's own suite is. That is `test-architecture/mc-test` in the memoro repository, and it is where the large numbers are — measured 2026-08-31, one path prefix draws 355 of a change's 395 test files, and removing it takes the run from 233.6 s to 21.1 s. This project cannot make that better and must not try.

Measurement B from `rulings.md` § 4 — a full suite run when the runner is idle, writing the repository's known red set. It existed to give the differential comparison something to subtract, and the comparison is gone. `--full` is the whole-suite reading now, and it is asked for rather than scheduled.

Whether `src/mc/red-ratchet.js` and its file survive at all. The verdict stops consulting it here; a standing red floor for main is a question about main, and this project has just been told that is not the round's business.
`mc merge`'s landing sequence, and the worktree form of the verb (no pull request). Ruling 4 settled that the PR form comes first.

success_criteria.criterion: A round runs the command gates the repository's selection reported.
success_criteria.check: `mc test memoro <pr>` on a pull request touching only `public/css/` shows `css:lint` and `css:tokens` in the verdict with their own timings; a branch with a deliberate `i18n:contract` violation comes back red naming that command. Both against a real pull request, not a fixture.

success_criteria.criterion: What to run for a repository is read from a declaration, and mc's shipped table is the fallback.
success_criteria.check: `declarationFor` returns a repository's own `.mc/test.json` fields over the shipped entry and under `~/mc/repo-gates.json`; `tests/mc/repo-gate-table.test.js` covers all three levels, an unparseable file is a stop with a reason, and a repository with no file produces a declaration byte-identical to today's.

success_criteria.criterion: No round builds or runs a baseline side.
success_criteria.check: `git grep -l 'repo-baseline-cache\|compareRed' -- src/` is empty, a round creates one worktree rather than two, and `mc test memoro <pr>` on a pull request whose affected set contains a test that is red on main comes back red naming that test.

success_criteria.criterion: `mc test <repo> --full` runs the whole suite and `mc test <repo> <pr>` never does.
success_criteria.check: `--full` runs the repository's declared suite command on one tree and reports its red names; the PR form's report names only files the selection chose. Both read off real runs.

success_criteria.criterion: The verdict is short enough to act on without reading twice.
success_criteria.check: A green round is at most three lines; a red one names the failing tests and commands and nothing else. Everything else moves behind `--json`. Judged on a real round of each kind, pasted into the pull request.

success_criteria.criterion: memoro-cli's own selector stops selecting a quarter of its suite for one documentation file.
success_criteria.check: `node scripts/affected-tests.js --base-ref origin/main` over a diff adding one file under `docs/project/` selects fewer than 10 test files, against the 57 of 250 measured on 2026-08-30.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: The round reads `files` and throws away `commands`
body: `selectFiles` in `src/mc/repo-gate.js` (around line 875 on main) takes `parsed?.files` and nothing else. `extra_gates` for memoro in `src/mc/repo-gate-table.js` is `Object.freeze([])`. So no contract gate runs in a round at all.

Measured 2026-08-31 in a memoro worktree: `node scripts/testing/ci.mjs --list --json --changed-path public/css/molecules/hero-card.css` reports 18 test files **and** `css:lint` and `css:tokens`. A round over that change runs the 18 and neither command.

On the real pull request #11158 the same selector reported six commands, and `npm run ci` timed each of them: `i18n:contract` 4.98 s, `i18n:locale-contract` 3.87 s, `i18n:validate` 0.25 s, `sdk:check` 1.65 s, `css:lint` 7.50 s, `css:tokens` 1.67 s. Twenty seconds. Martin approved exactly this set on 2026-08-31.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: The instruction may not be "run the repository's whole gate"
body: The obvious design — mc runs `npm run ci -- --base-ref <base>` and reads its `--json-report` — was measured and rejected. On #11158 it is **554.7 s**: 530.6 s of tests at memoro's own two-slot cap plus 20.0 s of commands. Martin, 2026-08-31: *"Full npm run ci ska vi inte köra. Det är för stort."*

The same 395 files run in 233.6 s when spawned the way `measureSelected` already spawns them — `node --test --test-reporter=tap` with no `--test-concurrency`, so Node's default of seven on this eight-core machine. So mc's own execution is already the faster of the two, and the instruction should keep it: list through the selector, run the list here, run the commands the selector named.

That has a cost mc must not hide. Because it does not go through memoro's runner, mc does not know a file's resource class — `printablePlan` in `ci.mjs` does not report one, even though `buildExecutionBatches` has them — so `sqlite` and `heavy` files have been running seven-wide in every round already. The memoro side of this work is adding that to the selection; until it does, the instruction declares which paths must not run in parallel, or it declares nothing and the round says so.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: `affected` is declared, normalised nowhere, read by dead code
body: `src/mc/repo-freshen.js:9` describes the freshen step as running the repository's declared `affected`. `normalise()` in `src/mc/repo-gate-table.js` returns `prepare`, `prepare_why`, `select`, `select_why`, `extra_gates`, `merge_log` and `pr_tests_flags` — and no `affected`. The field is `undefined` for every repository and that path has never run.

`rulings.md` § 4 declared memoro's `affected` as `npm run ci -- --base-ref origin/main` and memoro-cli's as `ownTests`. Neither is reachable. Adding the field is one line; what it should hold for memoro is now a different answer than the ruling gave, for the reason above.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: memoro-cli's own selector has memoro's disease, smaller
body: Measured 2026-08-30: adding a single file under `docs/project/mc/` made `node scripts/affected-tests.js --base-ref origin/main` select **57 of 250** test files. Every one of them carried the same reason — `reads:docs/project/mc/`. A directory prefix appearing in a test's source is being matched as a pin against a new file underneath it.

Running those 57 took about 41 s and gave 782 tests, 781 passing. The one failure, `tests/mc/canon.test.js` "reads all three packaged canon files from the real package", is red identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout.
It is the same shape as memoro's blanket and a quarter the size, and it is in this repository's own gate. Worth fixing here rather than pointing at the other repository's version of it.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: Ruling 4 is the design of record, and this plan carries it
body: `docs/project/mc/rulings.md` § 4, ruled 2026-08-29, raised as `mc-test-1`, owner `mc-test`. It says of itself: *"No `mc-test` plan exists. This ruling is not carried by any plan."*

The project directory is `mc-test-round` and not `mc-test` for a mechanical reason worth writing down: `repoOf` in `src/mc/run.js` is a literal `[memoro, memoro-cli]` and returns the first repository with a worktree in the workarea, and `runStep` then reads the plan out of *that* worktree. The `mc-test` workarea holds both checkouts, so a plan named `mc-test` in this repository is invisible to the runner — it looks in memoro, finds no plan, and skips. A plan named `mc-test` already existed here on 2026-08-30 and had exactly that fault; it is deleted by this project's first commit.

That is a defect in `run.js`, not only an inconvenience: a project knows which repository its plan was found in, and that should outrank directory order. It is not fixed here — it is named so the next person does not rediscover it by having a plan silently never run.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: The baseline side is half the round, and four modules
body: `runGate` builds two detached worktrees, runs `prepare` in each (memoro: `npm ci`, 7.8 s for a 492 MB `node_modules`), and runs the same file list in both. For pull request #11158 that is two × 233.6 s of tests — about eight minutes for one change.

The machinery around it is larger than the second run: `src/mc/repo-baseline-cache.js` carries a green baseline forward so it need not be rerun, `compareRed` in `tap-red.js` produces the `broke` set the verdict rests on, and `red-ratchet.js` is consulted for `baseline_risen`. All of it answers "was main already red?", and none of it survives the 2026-08-31 ruling.

Ruling 4's condition 1 stops mattering with the baseline: two truncated measurements can no longer match each other and read as "no new red", because there is only one measurement. It is still worth confirming that memoro's `scripts/testing/runner.mjs` runs every batch after a red one and that `tapTotals` sums every process's summary — a truncated single side under-reports red just as happily.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: The gates run, and what they cost on two real pull requests
body: Measured 2026-08-31 with `mc test memoro <pr>` against two throwaway pull requests opened for it and closed after. #11185, a css-only diff: the selection reported 17 test files **and** two commands, and the round ran them — `css:lint` 15.1 s, `css:tokens` 1.6 s, both green, against 7 s a side for the tests. #11186, one new file under `public/js/` with a hardcoded `textContent`: the selection reported 9 test files and three commands, `i18n:contract` failed in 4.0 s naming the file and the string, and the round came back red on it with 0 red tests on either side.

So the gates' cost profile is not the tests'. On #11185 the two commands took 17 s against 14 s for both suite runs together — `css:lint` is stylelint over the whole of `public/css/**`, not over the diff, so it does not shrink when the selection does. That is the shape to expect: a narrower selection makes the tests cheaper and leaves the commands where they are.

`css:lint` measured 15.1 s here against the 7.50 s `npm run ci` timed on #11158. Same command, same machine, twice the number — worth knowing before any decision rests on the 20.0 s figure in this plan's goal.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: memoro's own runner stops at the first failing command; mc no longer does
body: This step's instruction quotes `ci.mjs` as having chosen to run every command even after one fails. The comment it quotes is real — `runCi` runs `executeCommands` whether or not the tests passed — but it is about tests versus commands. Among the commands themselves, `executeCommands` in `scripts/testing/ci.mjs` ends its loop with `if (result.code !== 0 || result.signal) break;`.

mc follows the instruction rather than the code: every command the selection named runs, and the verdict reports all of them. #11186 is the evidence — `i18n:contract` failed, and `i18n:locale-contract` (5.6 s) and `i18n:validate` (0.3 s) still ran and still reported. On that pull request memoro's own runner would have shown one line where the round shows three.

That is a difference between two tools answering the same question, and it is the kind that goes unnoticed until somebody compares outputs. If the memoro side wants them to agree, `executeCommands` is the one line to change — and the round is the side that already behaves the way the comment describes.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: Three files answer one question, and only the repository's may fail loudly
body: The layers merge differently on purpose. `~/mc/repo-gates.json` keeps replacing an entry whole — the D-0135 rule, and its `shadowed` report — but `<repo>/.mc/test.json` merges field by field. A repository writes about itself and cannot know facts that are not its own: `merge_log` resolves under the work root on *this* machine, so a whole-entry replacement would make a file that says `select` drop the merge log in silence, which is the hole this table has already paid for twice.

The parse failures diverge for the same reason. A broken operator file still lets the shipped declaration answer (asserted since 2026-08-22) because it is additions on top of a declaration; a broken `.mc/test.json` is a stop, because falling back there would run the round on an instruction somebody believes they replaced.

The new door needed the old lock. A `.mc/test.json` saying only `select`, for a repository mc ships nothing for, would have meant `prepare: null` by omission — the guess the whole file refuses, arriving from the side. It stops unless the file states `prepare`, or the manifest proves there is nothing to install.

Two facts found while wiring it: `.mc/` already exists in this repository and holds `red-ratchet.json`, so the address sits beside one that is already there; and `declarationFor` is handed the repository path, not the candidate worktree, so a pull request cannot edit the instruction that judges it. Both are worth keeping that way.

`affected` and `serial_paths` are readable now and no shipped entry fills either. `affected` has no value to ship — ruling 4 said `npm run ci`, which is 554.7 s and was ruled out 2026-08-31. `serial_paths` distinguishes `null` (this repository has not said) from `[]` (it has said, and nothing is serial), which is what lets a round report the honest first one.

documents.label: The memoro half — what "affected" means, and where the large numbers are

steps.title: Run the command gates the selection already reported
steps.done_when: A round over a pull request touching only `public/css/` reports `css:lint` and `css:tokens` in its verdict with timings and pass/fail, and a branch with a deliberate `i18n:contract` violation comes back red naming that command.
instruction: `selectFiles` keeps `parsed?.files` and drops `commands`. Keep both. The commands are `{ id, packageScript, passBaseRef, resourceClass, selectedBy }`.

Run them on the **candidate only**, after the files, in the order the selector gave. They are gates about the change rather than measurements of two trees: `css:tokens` and `i18n:contract` take `--base-ref` and are differential in themselves, so running them on the baseline would measure main against main. Invoke exactly as memoro's own `runPackageCommand` does — `npm run <packageScript>`, plus `-- --base-ref <ref>` when `passBaseRef` is true.

Run every command even after one fails, and report all of them. `ci.mjs` made that choice explicitly and wrote down the reason: while any selected test is red, a skipped command gate hides every contract regression it would have caught. Copy the behaviour, not the code.

Report each in the verdict the way `report.extra_gates` already is — name, command, duration, ok — and make the round's `ok` depend on them. Keep `extra_gates` as a separate concept: that is what an operator declares beside the suite, this is what the repository's selector chose for this diff. One list, a field saying which is which.

Verify against a real memoro pull request touching `public/css/`, then contrive the negative. The whole set costs 20.0 s on the pull request measured — this step is cheap and it is the one that stops the gate lying about what it checked.

steps.title: The instruction the repository owns
steps.done_when: `declarationFor` reads `.mc/test.json` from the repository under test, layered shipped < repository file < `~/mc/repo-gates.json`; an unparseable file is a stop with a reason; a repository with no file behaves exactly as today; and `affected` is present in `normalise()`.
instruction: `src/mc/repo-gate-table.js` holds memoro's `prepare`, `select`, `pr_tests_flags` and `merge_log` in mc's own source, so every change to how memoro tests itself is a memoro-cli release. The file's header argues at length that what a repository needs must be *written down* rather than guessed; this step keeps the rule and moves the writing to where the repository can do it.

Add the third layer to `declarationFor`: `SHIPPED`, then `<repoPath>/.mc/test.json`, then `readOverrides(root)`. The operator's file stays the last word — it is how a machine-local fact gets in without a release. A file that will not parse is a stop with a reason and never a silent fall-through, because a partial declaration must stop exactly as hard as a missing one.
Report which layer each field came from, the way `shadowed` already names the fields an override dropped. A refusal has to tell the reader which of three files to edit.
Add `affected: entry.affected ?? null` to `normalise()` — one line, and `repo-freshen.js` has been describing a path that does not exist without it.

What the declaration should hold for memoro is not what ruling 4 assumed, and ruling 4's differential half was overruled on 2026-08-31. It is not `npm run ci`, which is 554.7 s and which Martin ruled out on 2026-08-31; it is the selector command that lists what the change reaches, the node flags to run that list with, and — until memoro's selection reports a resource class per file — the paths that must not run in parallel. Write the field for that last one even if memoro's file leaves it empty, so the honest answer "this repository has not said" is expressible.
Ship no `.mc/test.json` in memoro from here. The reader lands first and changes nothing on its own; memoro's file is a small pull request in that repository, which the memoro-side project can carry.
Cover all three precedence levels in `tests/mc/repo-gate-table.test.js`, plus the unparseable file, the partial file, and the no-file case asserting today's declaration byte for byte.

steps.title: Stop measuring the baseline at all
steps.done_when: A round builds one worktree, not two; `git grep -l 'repo-baseline-cache\|compareRed' -- src/` is empty; and a round on a pull request whose affected set contains a test that is red on main comes back red naming that test.
instruction: Ruled by Martin on 2026-08-31: a round evaluates the diff, and whether main was already red is not the round's question. This is the largest deletion in the project and it is also the 2× — the baseline side is half the wall clock, and on memoro it is also a second `npm ci` and a second worktree.

What goes. `runGate` builds `baseDir` beside `headDir`, runs `prepare` in both, runs `measureSelected` on both, and calls `compareRed(report.baseline.red, after.result.red)` — the `broke` set — the verdict. Remove the baseline worktree, its prepare, its suite run, `broke`, `fixed`, and the baseline halves of the extra-gate comparison around `compareRed(base.red, head.red)`. The verdict becomes: the candidate's red names, and the failing commands.

`src/mc/repo-baseline-cache.js` goes with it — `loadBaseline`, `carriedGate`, `loadMeasuredGate`, `saveMeasuredGate`, `lockfileHashAt`, and the `carried` branch in `runGate` that reports a baseline as measured when it was read from disk. It exists only to avoid rerunning a side that is no longer run.
`compareRed` in `src/mc/tap-red.js` loses its caller. Delete it with its test; keep `redNames` and `tapTotals`, which the one remaining side needs.

The ratchet consultation goes out of the verdict: `readRatchet`, `ratchetAtRef`, `compareRatchet` and the `baseline_risen` field all describe main's standing red, which is the question the ruling just removed. Do not delete `src/mc/red-ratchet.js` itself — whether a floor for main is worth keeping somewhere is a separate question, and this step's job is that the round stops asking it.

Say the consequence plainly in the pull request rather than discovering it later: a change whose affected tests include a test that is already red on main is now red, and cannot land until that test is green. That is stricter than today and it is the point. It is also why the memoro side's work matters — a narrowed selection reaches far fewer unrelated tests, so this bites much less often than it would have before.

Add `mc test <repo> --full`: the repository's declared suite command on the candidate tree, one side, reporting its red names. That is the only reading that is about the code rather than about a change, and it is asked for, never scheduled. `runFullSuite` and `measure` already exist for it; they lose their second side like everything else.

steps.title: Make the verdict short
steps.done_when: A green round is at most three lines and a red one names the failing tests and commands and nothing else; everything else moves behind `--json`; and `docs/technical/mc-merge.md` describes the round as it now is.
instruction: Ruled by Martin on 2026-08-31: do not hand the session information it has to take a position on. It costs tokens and turns a yes/no into a judgement call. The round's output today is the opposite — baseline counts, risen ratchet names, carried-baseline ages, the selector's admissions, per-gate deltas on two sides.

Most of it disappears with step 3, because it was describing the side that is gone. What remains has to be cut deliberately. Green: the repository, what was run (files and commands, as counts), and the time. Red: the failing test names and the failing commands, and the time. Nothing conditional, nothing the reader must weigh.

Keep the one admission that changes what the reader should do: when the selector could not narrow the change and fell back to the whole suite, the round says so in a clause, because it means the verdict is broader than the diff. Drop the blindness count — it is a fact about the selector, not about this change, and the reader can do nothing with it.

Everything cut stays available behind `--json`, which already exists as a flag. Phase timings, per-command durations and per-file cost belong there. Per-file cost cannot be parsed from what the round captures — a 395-file run produced 3,317 `duration_ms` lines and zero `ok N - tests/…` lines, so the TAP has no file attribution — so if it is wanted, take it from a small custom reporter on Node's test-runner events, which carry `data.file`. Only if it is wanted: it is diagnostics, and this step is about removing output, not adding it.

Rewrite the round's description in `docs/technical/mc-merge.md` to match: one side, the diff's tests, the selector's gates, `--full` for the whole suite. Delete the two-sided description rather than leaving it beside the new one; `repo-gate-table.js`'s header records what two places answering one question about one repository already cost here.

Replace the sentence in `docs/project/mc/rulings.md` § 4 that says no plan carries the ruling, and record there that its differential half was overruled on 2026-08-31 — the ruling stays readable, and a reader is not left believing the comparison still exists.

steps.title: Stop this repository's own selector matching a directory as a pin
steps.done_when: A diff adding one file under `docs/project/` selects fewer than 10 test files, against the 57 of 250 measured on 2026-08-30, and the tests that genuinely read a plan document are still among them.
instruction: Measured 2026-08-30: one new file under `docs/project/mc/` made `scripts/affected-tests.js` select 57 of this repository's 250 test files, every one with the reason `reads:docs/project/mc/`. The pin index is treating a directory prefix that appears in a test's source as a pin against every file underneath it.
That is the same defect as memoro's path-prefix blanket, a quarter the size, and in this repository's own gate. It is worth fixing here rather than only pointing at the other one.

A path literal that names a directory is a different fact from one that names a file. A test holding `'docs/project/mc/'` is almost always building a path or scanning a tree, not asserting on one document's text. Distinguish them — a pin resolves to a tracked *file*, a directory literal selects only when a rule says a test reads that tree — and keep the fail-closed half: a changed path the index cannot reason about must still select rather than silently not.

Verify both directions. The narrow case: adding one plan document selects the handful of tests that actually read plan documents, and `tests/architecture/plan-file-shape.test.js` had better be one of them. The wide case: changing a source file a test reads as text still selects that test — `merge-doc.test.js` asserting against `repo-gate.js`'s source is the example `repo-gate-table.js` names, and it must keep working.
Land the measurement: files selected before and after for the same one-document diff, and the reason list for each survivor.
